docs.purpose: The hand-off page between the mobile app and the payment provider. A user who taps subscribe in the app arrives here with a one-time code in the web address and no web login; the page trades that code for a payment page and sends the browser straight on to it, showing only a spinner while it works. If the code is missing, already used, or older than fifteen minutes, it shows one honest message telling the user to go back to the app and start again.
docs.data_story: It reads nothing from the database directly. Every value arrives through one contract: `/api/subscribe/exchange`. Behind that contract, the data comes from `logic_variables` and `user_profiles`, and writes land on `subscribe_nonces` and `user_profiles`.
docs.under_126: **REBUILD** — it drives writes, so a client decision has to be re-homed on the server before the projection can be honest. It renders through the WIZARD_STEP renderer (declared step index, advance condition, resume key and skip rule), reading by reference: `/api/subscribe/exchange`. It owns no component of its own, so its `owns.components[]` is an empty array — a legal answer, written down.

outputs.why: It POSTs the nonce and does nothing else — consumption, authorization and Stripe session creation are all server-side; the page holds no secret and makes no decision.
outputs.rollback: none — the nonce is single-use and consumed server-side; a failed exchange is unrecoverable from this page by design, and the app mints a fresh nonce instead.

state.why: One useState phase flag plus a useRef re-entry guard — both component-local, both gone on navigate; the ref exists because React 18 StrictMode would otherwise double-POST a single-use nonce.

staleness.why: It shows no server data — only a spinner or one error message; the exchange result is a redirect, not a rendered value.

session.why: /subscribe is in PUBLIC_PATHS and /api/subscribe/exchange is in PUBLIC_EXACT_API_PATHS — deliberately exact-match so the sibling /api/subscribe/session and /portal-session stay authenticated.

rls_class.why: Behind the contract the exchange resolves a user_profiles row — a user-owned table whose policies key on auth.uid(); the page reaches it only through the service-side handler, holding a nonce instead of a session.

disclosure.why: The only field this anonymous page receives is the Stripe-hosted checkout URL, and it is validated to start with https:// before being navigated to.

checks.why: The nonce is single-use, so the startedRef guard must survive StrictMode's double-invoked effect — a second POST consume-fails and strands a paying user on the error state.
window.location.assign is driven by a server-supplied string; the `url.startsWith("https://")` test is the only thing preventing this page from being an open redirect primitive.
Every non-200 — expired, consumed, unknown nonce, or a named config 500 — has to land on the one "invalid or expired" copy that tells the user to mint a fresh link, never on a blank spinner.

errors.why: One honest error state for every failure class: a full-page message telling the visitor to return to the app and mint a fresh link. The envelope is not parsed — only res.ok and the url shape are.

emits.why: No captureEvent, no ledger row — the handoff step of the paid funnel emits nothing, so a drop-off between the app's CTA and Stripe is invisible from this surface.

offers.why: A checkout handoff page renders no sponsored placement.

metering.why: The page writes no usage_events row; billing is Stripe's and the entitlement is the webhook's.

config.why: The page itself reads no tunable. The nonce TTL it describes ("expire after 15 minutes") is enforced server-side in the exchange route, not here — this copy is a claim about the route, not a value this page holds.

sharing.why: /api/subscribe/exchange is reached by this page and nothing else — the exact-match public listing exists precisely to keep it that narrow.

limitations.what: A configuration failure and an expired nonce are shown identically.
limitations.measured: src/app/subscribe/page.tsx:47-50 branches on res.ok only; the route's named 500s carry distinguishing codes that this page discards.
src/app/subscribe/page.tsx:85 and :101 use animate-spin with no prefers-reduced-motion arm anywhere in the file or in src/app/globals.css.

notes: The endpoint it calls, /api/subscribe/exchange, is itself in PUBLIC_EXACT_API_PATHS (exact-match, checked before the '/api/subscribe' authenticated prefix) precisely so a sessionless hand-off visitor can reach it; sibling routes such as /api/subscribe/session stay authenticated. A startedRef guard stops React StrictMode's double-invoke from consuming the single-use code twice. MEASURED 2026-09-15. The WIZARD_STEP profile's step_index/advances_on/resume_key/skip_when/terminal fields have no home in the current schema (it declares no wizard block), so they are recorded here instead: step 1 of 2 in the web half of the handoff; advances_on = a 200 carrying an https:// url; resume_key = none, the nonce is single-use and a resume mints a fresh one from the app; skip_when = never; terminal = false (Stripe returns the visitor to /subscribe/success or /subscribe/cancel). The page copy says "Return to the Buildo app" while the estate is mid-rename to MaxBLD (layout.tsx:6) — the same half-applied Spec 117 rename the landing page carries.

measured_gate.why: classifyRoute('/subscribe') is NOT caught by the AUTHENTICATED_API_ROUTES arm (that list's '/api/subscribe' entry only matches '/api/subscribe' or '/api/subscribe/...'), no PUBLIC_PREFIXES entry is a prefix of it, and it then matches the PUBLIC_PATHS exact list which contains '/subscribe' -> 'public'.

programme.why: The subscription and Stripe hand-off, which resolves an entitlement per PRODUCT — so it serves both and belongs to neither.
